answer.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing is an acute, revenue-threatening event targeting price-sensitive SMB accounts—exactly the segment memory_73 addresses with strong acquisition/revenue lift and reduced time-to-value. This is the most consequential and time-sensitive lever, so I want to verify its original record before committing capacity to it, especially since discounting carries risk to long-term margin and perceived value that the consolidated summary may understate. I'm also verifying memory_86 (onboarding simplification) because onboarding completion is independently down 4% QoQ, and I want to check whether the archived record shows the improvement held across cohorts or was context-specific, since it's a plausible alternative or complementary action. Given only one experiment slot and two live problems (competitive pricing pressure and eroding onboarding/activation), I'm prioritizing the more urgent revenue-defense action but running it as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, since promotional pricing responses can create downstream expectations or margin erosion that aren't captured in a short-term acquisition/revenue metric. This preserves optionality to address onboarding/activation decline next cycle if this test doesn't resolve the competitive threat.
